key_insight: MediX-R1 uses group-based reinforcement learning and a composite, clinically calibrated reward to fine-tune multimodal LLMs so they produce clinically grounded, free-form medical answers rather than being limited to multiple-choice formats.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between evaluation-friendly multiple-choice tasks and real-world clinical needs by enabling medically accurate, semantically robust free-form responses from vision-language medical models.
method: Fine-tune a baseline vision–language backbone for medical multimodal input.
Apply Group Based Reinforcement Learning to stabilize fine-tuning across diverse clinical cases.

Optimize a composite reward: (a) an LLM-based accuracy reward that enforces a strict YES/NO semantic correctness judgment, and (b) a medical embedding–based semantic reward to reward faithful paraphrases and semantic equivalence.
impact: Provides a practical training framework for developers of medical MLLMs to produce clinically reliable, open-ended answers—improving real-world usability, interpretability, and evaluation of clinical reasoning in multimodal models.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram: vision–language backbone + Group Based RL loop + composite reward modules.
Reward composition infographic: split showing LLM-based YES/NO accuracy and medical-embedding semantic reward with examples.
Before/After QA examples: multiple-choice limited output vs. MediX-R1 free-form clinically grounded answer.
Performance charts: semantic accuracy and robustness (paraphrase acceptance) gains across clinical benchmarks.
paper_title: MediX-R1: Open Ended Medical Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Sahal Shaji Mullappilly, Mohammed Irfan Kurpath, Omair Mohamed, Mohamed Zidan, Fahad Khan
